result:
If I could change the world in one way, I would eliminate the illusion of separation—the belief that we are fundamentally divided by borders, beliefs, identities, or interests. I would replace it with a deep, unshakable understanding that every human being is interconnected, that suffering in one part of the world echoes in another, and that our collective well-being depends on recognizing our shared humanity.

This wouldn’t erase differences—cultures, ideas, and perspectives would still thrive—but it would dissolve the fear, greed, and violence that arise from seeing others as "other." It would prioritize empathy over exploitation, cooperation over competition, and long-term sustainability over short-term gain.

In essence, I’d want to rewire the human mind to see the world not as a collection of isolated entities, but as a single, breathing organism where harm to one is harm to all. And from that shift, everything else—justice, peace, environmental stewardship—would follow more naturally.
